Poinciana (APV) Design Control Board: driveways, walks, patios and pavers

Published 2026-09-10 · Last reviewed 2026-09-11 · By the Kissimmee Concrete team

Association of Poinciana Villages

What the Poinciana DCB requires for driveways, walks and patios

From the Poinciana Villages Design Control Board Criteria (March 18, 2021): '9.1.1 Driveways and Walks. Concrete, asphalt, or brick pavers will be characteristic of the driveways required. Walks shall be of the same materials unless otherwise approved by the DCB. Any walkway adjacent to the residence dwelling must not exceed two (2) feet in width.' And: 'No building, fence, driveway, patio, drainage, paved area, wall or any other structure shall be commenced, erected, or maintained' without the DCB's prior written approval.

How we handle a Poinciana job

  1. Site visit; we photograph the existing driveway and measure its width, because the Criteria tie new work to the existing width requirement.
  2. DCB application with site plan, material, color and dimensions; you sign as owner. Like-for-like concrete replacements are routine but still required.
  3. Follow-up before day 30; silence is a denial under 6.1.
  4. County permit: Osceola driveway permit (§22-50.6) for Osceola villages, Polk rules for Polk villages; the finder shows which.
  5. Work; DCB copy of the permit number on request.

Solivita, inside Poinciana's boundaries but with its own association, uses its own ARC: Solivita. City page: Poinciana; permits: Unincorporated Osceola County, Polk County (unincorporated).

Process

The thirty-day clock, and why it is the important clause

Most architectural provisions are about what you may build. The clause worth planning around in Poinciana is about time: under the published Design Control Board criteria, an application that has not been acted on within thirty days is deemed disapproved rather than approved. Silence is a denial.

That inverts the normal assumption. In many communities an applicant who hears nothing assumes tacit consent and proceeds; here that produces work without approval, which the association can require to be removed. So the process we follow is to submit a complete packet, obtain written confirmation of receipt, diary the thirtieth day, and follow up in good time before it. An incomplete application that sits waiting for a missing sample is the common way the clock runs out.

What the criteria say about surfaces

The criteria name concrete, asphalt and brick pavers as the driveway materials, and require walks to be of the same materials unless the board approves otherwise. Any walkway adjacent to the dwelling is limited to two feet in width without approval. Pavers are required to finish flush with the connecting driveway, walkway or roadway, which on a replacement means excavating deeper rather than building up. Prior written approval is required before any driveway, patio, drainage work or paved area is begun. And the owner is responsible for keeping driveways, walks and patios clean and maintained.

Read together, those provisions are more permissive on material than people expect and stricter on dimension and process than people expect. A paver driveway is straightforward to approve; a wider walk beside the house is not.

Questions we get about this

Can I use pavers on my driveway in Poinciana?

Brick pavers are an accepted driveway material under 9.1.1, with prior written DCB approval.

How wide can my front walk be?

A walkway adjacent to the house may not exceed 2 feet unless the DCB approves otherwise.

What if the DCB doesn't respond?

After 30 days the application is deemed disapproved; resubmit or follow up.

Do I need approval to replace my driveway with the same concrete?

Yes; the Criteria require prior written approval for any driveway work.
